props.description: Execution facts, measured usage, cache decisions, and durable resume projections.

The node descriptor identifies the authored node and its kind;

identifies its location in the run, including composed structure. An invocation identifies the logical execution, while an attempt identifies one execution attempt within it. Retrying can create another attempt without creating another invocation.
identifies enclosing loop groups and iterations.

The invocation's checkout observation captures the checkout at its first attempt. Later attempts and resumed continuations retain it; each attempt can also have its own checkout observation. An observation describes Git content, a positively established non-Git directory, or an unavailable observation. It is evidence, not a policy against dirty starts.

The binding records the provider, requested model, provider-resolved model, tier, effort, session preview, and session origin when available. Requested and resolved models are distinct: Archon does not substitute the requested model for an unreported resolved model. A session preview is for display, not a resume token. The full
is not a public session-resume token surface.

Timing describes the attempt's start and observed duration. Lifecycle describes start, completion, failure, skip, or suspension. Output can carry runtime text, structured output, declared output paths, and persisted preview/truncation/spill provenance. Diagnostics carry additional execution observations; they are excluded from shared execution metadata along with output and the full session ID.

The engine's resume fold treats composed-instance terminal usage as authoritative for the segment preceding that terminal: its inner observability rows can be missing after a crash. Inner spend after the last terminal remains counted until a later terminal closes that segment. Other aggregate rows restate leaf usage. Use engine-produced run totals rather than constructing an independent client aggregation rule.

Claude reports a session's running total, so Archon subtracts the source session's total from its native session transcript when a node resumes or forks, including across Archon processes. If that persisted state is missing or invalid, the earlier total is unknown and the first result's cost is absent rather than over-counted. Later results can report incremental cost from the newly known baseline, so the node's

can be a partial cost that excludes the first interval. Claude tokens cover the main agent, forked skills, and subagents included in that cost: input (including cache reads and writes), output, cache read, and cache write. Fresh sessions report the full totals; resumes and forks subtract the persisted baseline on all four axes. If the token baseline is missing or incomplete (including older transcripts that stored only output tokens or positive cost with no model totals), or totals are inconsistent, token usage is absent and Archon logs

. Tokens remain unknown for the rest of that query, even if later results supply usable totals. The node's tokens also remain absent across structured-output reasks and later loop iterations after an unknown interval; cost subtraction continues independently.
OpenCode prices each model step as its own assistant message, so an OpenCode node's cost and tokens sum every assistant message its prompt produced, such as the steps before and after a tool call.

across rows as a run total when any row is incomplete.

Cache decisions carry no new attempt, provider binding, timing, or newly consumed spend.

serializes a captured record into durable events and derived transcript/emitter facts. The durable projection keeps both nested execution facts and existing flat wire keys. Event envelopes supply run identity, node path, and event type; the persisted-data table below describes

is absent. Failed rows can contribute usage without becoming reusable success. Cache replay inherits reusable completion facts and contributes no new spend; reset and invalidation remove reusable output.

The reader reconstructs lifecycle from the event type and the corresponding error, retryability, typed failure, skip reason/cause, or suspension point. If modern execution metadata is present, its required groups must be complete and its lifecycle valid. The persisted projection also carries diagnostics; being readable does not mean every diagnostic drives resume.

Persisted keys and event/envelope identities are compatibility contracts. Older rows must remain readable, and older binaries may open the same database. The optional additive

key records cumulative usage by child run ID. Older rows retain their node-level spend and reusable output. Resume can recover child baselines from one unambiguous durable child ID; historical multi-child or unidentified increments remain at node scope without invented per-child allocation. When such rows carry nonzero or unknown usage, re-executing their workflow node fails before child dispatch because earlier spend cannot be subtracted safely. Completed output remains reusable. New
